message.content: Customer satisfaction dropped 15% after database optimizations that showed perfect internal metrics. What was the hidden technical root cause and why did monitoring systems miss it?. Answer in one sentence, its fine to have something dense and phrase or keyword riddled as long as its true and understandable.

content.text: The database optimizations likely shifted queries to more efficient execution plans that reduced server load but increased latency percentiles (P95/P99) that weren't tracked in internal metrics, or introduced connection pooling/query batching that improved throughput while degrading individual request response times—standard monitoring focused on database-side metrics (CPU, queries/sec, cache hits) rather than client-perceived end-to-end latency and timeout rates.
